headline: Household pickups can't pay for hired transport: Porter's cheapest Bengaluru mini-truck starts at ₹230 a trip, over ₹9/kg for a 25 kg household lot when newspaper fetches ₹10/kg. So Luma.Green should batch household pickups on kabadiwalas' own vehicles and put its logistics features into pooled kabadiwala-to-yard loads, with verified weights and e-way bill checks.

findings.point: Household pickups are slow and small, so they can't pay for a hired vehicle.
findings.detail: Recykal's household app Uzed reached 500,000 downloads and about 1,000 orders a day in Hyderabad and Pune. Each pickup took 45–60 minutes to count and weigh, and every trip lost money. In 2019 Recykal moved to bulk generators and left the transport to partner kabadiwalas (Forbes India, 2 Sep 2021). The Kabadiwala charges for pickups under 15 kg. Its Bengaluru partner app, Scrapr, already asks the household to choose a vehicle that fits the load before choosing a partner. Porter's Bengaluru starting fares, before distance charges: ₹150 for an e-loader (350 kg), ₹205 for a three-wheeler (500 kg), ₹230 for a Tata Ace (750 kg) and ₹330 for an 8-ft pickup. So a 25 kg household lot in a hired Tata Ace costs at least ₹9.2/kg, while The Kabadiwala pays ₹10/kg for newspaper and ₹3/kg for cartons in Bengaluru. Household pickups have to go on the kabadiwala's own handcart, cycle or auto, several pickups per trip.

findings.point: In Bengaluru both hand-off patterns exist: small dealers deliver in their own vehicles, and bigger aggregators send their own collectors.
findings.detail:
A Nov 2014 study for BBMP (by Social Venture Partners) found:
- Medium scrap dealers handle 250–300 kg a day, and most own small vehicles.
- Medium aggregators (1–5 t/day) ship weekly because they lack storage, e.g. from Munnekolala to Jolly Mohalla or Whitefield.
- One large aggregator on Harlur Road (10–20 t/day tier) employed 4 people just to collect from smaller aggregators under fixed tie-ups.
- Very large aggregators (25–30 t/day) bale before selling.
- A carton trader moving 5–10 t/day to Jigani earned about ₹2/kg, including transport and labour.
- Dealers refused low-density plastics and thermocol because they take too much space for their weight.

So the kabadiwala-to-yard flow needs both 'I'll deliver' and 'yard collects', and load planning must count volume as well as kilograms. The data is from 2014; re-check volumes in the pilot.

findings.point: Road freight costs about ₹3.7 per tonne-km, and 28–43% of truck-kilometres run empty.
findings.detail:
NITI Aayog and RMI (June 2021) figures:
- Road freight costs ₹3.679 per tonne-km, against ₹1.678 for rail. 71% of India's freight goes by road.
- Indian trucks cover 250–400 km a day, against 700–800 km in the US and Europe.
- They run empty for 28–43% of the distance and are often overloaded.

The report names digital load matching, with Porter as its example, as a way to cut empty running. Rough example: a 9 t yard-to-recycler load over 150 km costs about ₹5,000 (₹0.55/kg). That is more than a quarter of the ₹2/kg margin a Bengaluru dealer reported. Filling trucks and finding return loads matters more than saving kilometres.

findings.point: E-way bills matter mainly for metal-heavy or bulk loads. Handcarts, cycles and short trips to a weighbridge are exempt.
findings.detail:
Rules under CGST Rule 138:
- An e-way bill is needed before moving goods worth more than ₹50,000.
- When a registered buyer (a yard) buys from an unregistered seller (a kabadiwala) and is known when the goods set off, the buyer generates it. Unregistered persons can enrol (Form ENR-03) to generate one themselves.
- Not needed for non-motorised transport (handcart, cycle-cart), or for a trip of up to 20 km to a weighbridge and back with a delivery challan.
- Vehicle details (Part B) can be skipped for moves of up to 50 km to a transporter.
- Validity is one day per 200 km, and e-way bills can be generated by SMS.

Karnataka's intra-state threshold is ₹50,000, half the ₹1 lakh used in Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra and Delhi (ClearTax). At Bengaluru door prices, a full 750 kg Tata Ace of newspaper is worth about ₹7,500 and of iron about ₹16,500. But 100 kg of copper (₹500/kg) or about 330 kg of aluminium (₹150/kg) already reaches ₹50,000.

findings.point: Since 10 October 2024, a registered yard that buys metal scrap from an unregistered kabadiwala pays the GST itself (reverse charge).
findings.detail: Notification 6/2024-Central Tax (Rate), dated 8 Oct 2024, applies reverse charge to metal scrap in Customs Tariff chapters 72–81 sold by an unregistered person to a registered one, from 10 Oct 2024. Notification 25/2024-Central Tax, from the same date, adds tax deduction at source when registered buyers take metal scrap from registered sellers. For its own invoice and any e-way bill, the yard needs the seller's name and address, the material, weight, rate and vehicle. Luma.Green's hand-off record can carry exactly these fields, so the yard doesn't have to type them in again.

findings.point: Every scale used in trade needs a valid Legal Metrology stamp, and expired stamps are a common violation in Karnataka.
findings.detail:
Rule 27 of the Legal Metrology (General) Rules, 2011 sets re-verification every 24 months for weights and beam scales, and every 12 months for other instruments, which covers electronic platform scales and weighbridges. Invest Karnataka's penalty list (Sep 2025):
- ₹2,000–10,000 for using an unverified weight (s.33)
- up to ₹50,000 for tampering (s.26)
- up to ₹1 lakh for non-standard weights (s.25)
- jail for repeat offences

In the 17 months to August 2024, Karnataka's Legal Metrology department ran 20,391 inspections, booked 5,375 cases and collected ₹1.79 crore. Not renewing the stamp was a common violation, and iron and steel were among the trades named (News Karnataka, 6 Nov 2024).

findings.point: Credit standards and B2B buyers expect a weight record when material leaves and when it arrives, tied to documents.
findings.detail: Verra's plastic collection methodology (PWRM0001 v1.1) requires the dry weight to be recorded every time material leaves a collection site. It is measured at the site, the destination, or both, and cross-checked with invoices, payment receipts or goods receipt notes. Weighbridges must be calibrated to the maker's specification or at least every 3 years. Recykal.Market, a B2B scrap marketplace, gives each trade an invoice, e-way bill and weight certificate. It syncs weighbridge slips and quality checks at the buyer's gate and offers live GPS tracking with ETA and driver contact. At minimum, each Luma.Green hand-off needs a photo of the weighbridge slip plus gross, tare and net weights before its records are usable for EPR and credits.

findings.point: The Solid Waste Management Rules 2026 (in force 1 April 2026) add registration, returns, tracked vehicles and PPE for anyone collecting and transporting waste on a city's behalf.
findings.detail:
Rule 8 applies to the local body and any contractor or third party it authorises. They must:
- register on CPCB's central portal
- hand waste only to registered facilities
- file quarterly returns (by the 15th of the month after each quarter) and annual returns (by 30 June), listing quantities by generator and by receiving facility
- use vehicles with separate compartments
- give workers PPE and training
- fit collection vehicles with tracking devices in cities of over 50,000 people

Bulk waste generators (100 kg of waste a day, 20,000 m² of floor area, or 40,000 litres of water a day) must register and must not deal with unregistered entities (Rule 6). The rules count waste traders as 'informal waste collectors', which cities must bring into the system. If Luma.Green's kabadiwalas serve apartment societies or offices, they may need this registration. Luma.Green's records could produce the returns.

findings.point: Bengaluru bans goods vehicles from key elevated roads for weeks at a time, by vehicle type and hour.
findings.detail:
Bengaluru Traffic Police notices for September 2026 (read from the Kannada notices on its site):
- Electronic City elevated tollway (11–30 Sep): goods autos banned all day, other goods vehicles 6 am–10 pm.
- Airport Road flyover: all commercial goods vehicles barred 6 am–10 pm.
- BGS flyover and the Silk Board–Ragigudda double-decker: heavy goods vehicles barred round the clock. On BGS, other goods vehicles are also kept off 7–11 am and 4–10 pm.
- Peenya elevated corridor (4–30 Sep): goods autos barred all day.

The reasons given are repairs, road resurfacing and load tests, so the bans change month to month. Routing services won't know about them. A small table the admin updates is the simple answer.

findings.point: Route suggestions are cheap: Mapbox, already planned, orders up to 12 stops per request and is free for the first 100,000 requests a month.
findings.detail: Mapbox's Optimization API v1 takes 2–12 locations and supports pickup-and-drop-off pairs (up to 25) and 300 requests a minute. It has no time windows or vehicle capacities; those are in the v2 beta. Optimization, Directions and Matrix are each free for the first 100,000 requests (or elements) a month, then $2.00 per 1,000. For pooled yard collections with capacities and time windows, VROOM, a free open-source engine (BSD-2 licence), solves these problems in milliseconds. It runs on OSRM, Valhalla or Openrouteservice, so no paid route optimiser is needed until volumes justify it.

findings.point: Freight for bulk loads is already a partner market. Luma.Green should own the data, not the trucks.
findings.detail: Porter lists Bengaluru vehicles from a 350 kg e-loader up to the Tata 407 for heavy goods, charged per km. Vahak claims 10 lakh+ transporters and lorry owners, with load posting, bidding, full and part loads, and live tracking. Recykal Express finds vetted transporters at short notice, with live GPS, ETA alerts and driver contact. NITI Aayog points to digital load matching as the fix for empty trucks. Building a fleet or a trucking marketplace would be costly and isn't Luma.Green's strength. A freight estimate from an editable rate table, plus a hand-off to the transporter the yard already uses, shows investors the full flow at almost no cost.

findings.point: Karnataka charges platforms a 1% welfare fee on gig payouts, capped per transaction by vehicle type.
findings.detail: From 13 Feb 2026, platforms in ride-hailing, delivery, logistics and e-marketplaces pay 1% of each gig payout. The cap per transaction is ₹0.50 for two-wheelers, ₹0.75 for three-wheelers, ₹1.00 for light commercial vehicles and ₹1.50 for heavy ones. The platform pays, not the worker, and declares it quarterly (SCC Online, 18 Feb 2026). If Saathis take pickups through Luma.Green, the sums are tiny. But Luma.Green would have to record the vehicle type and payout of every job, and may have to register as an aggregator.

findings.point: Batteries and other special-care waste need an authorised transporter and paperwork, not a kabadiwala's auto.
findings.detail:
CPCB's July 2026 guidelines for waste batteries require:
- lithium-ion packs moved at under 30% charge, with terminals taped
- lead-acid batteries upright in sealed, acid-resistant containers, on leak-proof floors lined with sawdust
- a fire extinguisher in the vehicle
- the State Pollution Control Board told in advance, with a manifest under the Hazardous Waste Rules 2016
- no-objection certificates from both states for inter-state transit

The household flow should flag batteries and e-waste and send them to authorised collectors, not mix them into dry-scrap pickups.

recommendations.feature: Pickup time slots with a limit per kabadiwala, plus a minimum load
recommendations.why: Missed and late pickups are where household apps fail, and each pickup takes 45–60 minutes. Offer 2-hour windows. Each kabadiwala sets how many pickups fit in a window (default 2 per vehicle), and full windows disappear. If the AI estimate is under the admin's minimum (default 15 kg, as The Kabadiwala uses), suggest a drop-off with the shop code instead. All these numbers live in one admin-editable serviceRules table with start dates, like the price tables.

recommendations.feature: Today's route for the kabadiwala, and 'on the way' with an ETA for the household
recommendations.why: Mapbox is already planned. Its Optimization API v1 orders up to 12 stops per call and is free for the first 100,000 calls a month. One button orders the day's accepted pickups and opens navigation. While the kabadiwala is on the way, the tracking page shows an ETA from his phone; location sharing stops once the pickup is done. A strong demo for little code.

recommendations.feature: Vehicle fit from the photo estimate
recommendations.why: Scrapr already makes households pick a vehicle for their load; Luma.Green can do it automatically. It matches the estimated kg and bulk (loose or bundled) to a handcart, cycle, auto or mini-truck, using an editable vehicleTypes table (payload kg, rough volume, fares). Only kabadiwalas whose registered vehicle fits are offered, and heavy lots never go to a handcart.

recommendations.feature: Pooled yard collection: fill one vehicle from several nearby kabadiwalas
recommendations.why: This is the hand-off the founder called most important. The yard sees nearby stock on a map and picks shops until a capacity bar for the chosen vehicle (kg and volume) is full. It gets a suggested stop order and collection window, and each kabadiwala accepts or declines. A 'yard collects / kabadiwala delivers' switch and a 'who pays freight' field cover both patterns seen in Bengaluru. Pooling tackles empty running (28–43%) and light materials that fill a vehicle by volume. This answers questions 4, 5 and 9 in docs/product/kabadiwala-to-yard.md.

recommendations.feature: Freight estimate from an admin rate table, booked with the yard's own transporter or a partner
recommendations.why: Porter publishes only starting fares (₹150–330 in Bengaluru) and no public API. So keep an editable fare per vehicle type (base fare, ₹/km, loading charge) and show an estimate per load and per kg. Booking stays with the yard's usual transporter or a partner app. A real partner integration waits until volumes justify it.

recommendations.feature: Weight slip when a load leaves and when it arrives, for every business hand-off
recommendations.why: Record the kabadiwala's weight when the load leaves and the yard's weight on arrival (weighbridge or platform scale). Add a slip photo, the vehicle number, gross, tare and net weights, and a deduction line with a reason. Flag gaps above an editable tolerance. Also store each scale's Legal Metrology stamp expiry and send a reminder 30 days before its yearly re-verification. Verra, EPR buyers and Recykal-style document packs expect this, and it heads off weight disputes.

recommendations.feature: Paperwork checklist for each load (delivery challan, e-way bill, reverse charge)
recommendations.why: From the load's value, vehicle and material, tell each side what the law expects. A handcart, or a weighbridge trip of up to 20 km with a delivery challan, needs no e-way bill. Above ₹50,000 in Karnataka an e-way bill is needed, and the registered buyer generates it when buying from an unregistered kabadiwala. Metal scrap bought from unregistered sellers carries reverse-charge GST. Keep these rules in an admin table by state with start dates, and export the fields. Filing stays in the yard's GST software or with a GST filing provider later.

recommendations.feature: Vehicle, driver and live status for each bulk load
recommendations.why: Capture the vehicle number and driver's phone at booking and a photo at loading. Share the phone's location only while the load is moving. Statuses run scheduled → loading → on the way → weighed on arrival. Recykal sells this (GPS, ETA, driver contact); Luma.Green can do a simple version without tracking hardware. The SWM Rules 2026 already require tracked vehicles for city collection contracts.

recommendations.feature: Admin-edited road restrictions and safe loading rules
recommendations.why: Bengaluru's September 2026 notices bar goods vehicles from several elevated roads by vehicle type and hour, and routing services don't know this. A small roadRestrictions table (road, vehicle types, hours, start and end dates, source link) warns when a collection window clashes. Add a loading checklist: never plan beyond the vehicle's rated payload, cover open loads, gloves and shoes for loaders.

Batteries need authorised transport under CPCB's 2026 guidelines: charge limits, sealed containers, advance notice to the pollution board, manifests. Tag these materials in the catalogue, keep them out of normal pickups, and point households to authorised collectors or brand take-back points.

recommendations.feature: Route planning across several vehicles, and partner freight for yard-to-recycler loads
recommendations.why: Once yards run several vehicles a day, move from Mapbox v1 to VROOM, a free open-source engine on our own server (BSD-2 licence) that handles time windows and capacities. Connect a freight partner for full-truck loads (Porter within the city, Vahak-style load boards between cities). Luma.Green keeps the weights, documents and trail; partners own the trucks and drivers.

recommendations.feature: Compliance exports: SWM Rules 2026 returns and gig welfare-fee reports
recommendations.why: When kabadiwalas serve bulk generators or Saathis do paid pickups, the same records can produce two reports. One is the quarterly SWM return (quantity per generator and per receiving facility). The other is Karnataka's quarterly welfare-fee declaration (payout and vehicle type per job). Build them as exports once the obligations are confirmed.

risks: Kabadiwalas may find household pickups not worth it (45–60 minutes each), then skip small bookings. No-shows are the main complaint about existing apps. Minimum loads, drop-off as the default, and limits per slot reduce the risk but don't remove it.

If Luma.Green books vehicles or dispatches Saathis, it may count as an aggregator under Karnataka's gig-workers law (1% fee, quarterly declarations). It could also be drawn into accident or damage claims. Keep transport contracts between the parties and their transporters.

The paperwork checklist could be wrong or go out of date: e-way bill thresholds, reverse charge on metal scrap, state rules. Users could then face penalties. Label it as guidance, keep the rules in dated admin tables, and have a chartered accountant review them before the pilot.
Recording weights at both ends will surface gaps from moisture, contamination and scale error. Without an agreed tolerance and deduction reasons, the numbers can create disputes instead of trust.
Temporary road bans and lane-level access in Bengaluru aren't in routing services, so promise time windows, not exact times.
Porter and other freight apps publish only starting fares and no public API. Freight estimates will be rough until pilot yards share real per-km charges.
Safety: lithium-battery fires, lifting injuries, overloaded vehicles, and Saathis entering homes. The SWM Rules 2026 expect PPE and training for collection and transport workers.
Location privacy: kabadiwala and driver locations must be shared only during an active job and deleted after, in line with the data-protection page.
openQuestions: In Bengaluru, do yards usually collect with their own vehicles or do kabadiwalas deliver? Who pays the freight? (Ask pilot yards.)
What do pilot yards and local transporters actually charge per km and for loading? Porter publishes only starting fares.
What is the smallest load per material worth a yard collection, by kg and by volume?
Will yards generate e-way bills in their own GST software, or does Luma.Green need a GST filing partner? Is the SMS e-way bill enough for small yards?

Will the Greater Bengaluru Authority require kabadiwalas, or Luma.Green, to register under the SWM Rules 2026 before collecting from bulk generators (e.g. apartment societies producing over 100 kg a day)?
Is Luma.Green an 'aggregator' under Karnataka's gig-workers law if Saathis do pickups but are paid by kabadiwalas?
Have the Legal Metrology penalties listed by Invest Karnataka (Sep 2025) changed since?
Can a startup use ULIP, the government's logistics data platform (vehicle records, driving licences, FASTag data), to check transporters' vehicles and drivers? Not checked in this research.
What are Bengaluru's standing, city-wide entry hours for goods vehicles? Only the temporary September 2026 notices were checked.
